subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinTechCo)

Subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinTechCo)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we can align on next steps. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Summary of pain points
- Recent production incidents have increased confidence concerns for LLM-powered features; primary impact is customer-facing latency and occasional degraded outputs.
- You need predictable behavior under partial infra failures (region/network blips) and controlled fallbacks so SLAs remain intact.
- Visibility into per-request cost and token-level tracing is important for your finance and platform teams.

Current stack (as you described)
- Primary: managed LLM endpoints hosted in one cloud region (us-west-2)
- No dedicated GPU pool today; relying on on-demand endpoints with autoscale
- Basic CDN + edge caching for non-model assets; no prefix/KV caching for model responses yet

Success criteria (what FinTechCo will consider successful)
- <99.9% availability for inference endpoints (SLO target) with clear RTO for failures
- Graceful degradation: automated fallback to cheaper/quantized model variants or alternate region within 60s for outage scenarios
- Audit logs and token-level cost breakdown available for monthly reviews

Incident history you mentioned
- Two customer-impacting incidents in Q4 2025 (brief outages affecting inference for ~20-30 minutes each) — priority to understand root causes and mitigations.

Our proposed approach / next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (1hr) — focus on runbooks, failover topology, and SLO/SLA options (Jonas to lead)
2) Provide an incident summary & draft SLA examples — I'll share a short packet (SLA + incident summary) by Wed 6/3
3) Procurement intro & draft commercial terms — include Mike Jensen for any procurement questions

Suggested times for the tech deep-dive (Pacific):
- Wed 6/9 10:00-11:00am
- Thu 6/10 2:00-3:00pm

Attachments I will send alongside the packet: redwood-reliability-sla.pdf (draft SLA examples), incident-summary-2025.csv (incident timeline + mitigation notes).

If that looks right, I'll schedule the deep-dive with Jonas and send the packet.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule: 

1) On availability: our internal bar for production features is 99.95% but we know inference-heavy paths are tougher. Can you share what SLOs Redwood typically recommends vs. what you can commit to in an SLA?

2) Incident details: can you summarize the root cause of the Q4 outages you referenced in the packet? Our ops team needs specifics to connect to our internal RCA process.

3) Failover options: are fallbacks limited to alternate regions, or do you support model-level fallbacks (e.g., a quantized local model or smaller variant) that keep responses degraded but functional?

4) Attachments: please send the packet (SLA + incident CSV) and any runbook excerpts we can share with our platform team.

We're good to loop Mike in on procurement after the technical deep-dive. Available next week — Thu 6/10 2pm PT works on our side if that slot is still free.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation (FinTechCo)

Hi Sarah — quick technical response and what we'll include in the packet. Happy to cover these in the deep-dive as well.

SLOs & SLA options
- Typical Redwood default SLO: 99.9% availability for hosted endpoints with best-effort regional failover.
- Enterprise SLA: configurable to 99.95% with reserved capacity (Redwood Dedicated) + financial credits for breaches; requires committed throughput.
- We'll include example SLA language and observability metrics (p99 latency, error budget burn rate, incident classification).

Incident summary (Q4 2025) — brief:
- Two incidents:
  1) 2025-10-18: Region-network partition in us-west-2 caused control-plane to lose connectivity to a subset of nodes; automated autoscaling re-provisioning took ~22 mins to restore steady-state traffic distribution. Impact: increased latency and 5-10% error rate for affected endpoints.
  2) 2025-11-29: Third-party GPU host driver regression during a rolling kernel update caused model processes to restart in a few clusters; root cause was upstream driver incompatibility. Impact: ~30 mins of degraded throughput; mitigations: pinned driver versions + proactive canary updates implemented.

Mitigations we deploy (summary)
- Multi-tier fallbacks: prefix/KV caching for common prompts (reduces token load), model-tier fallback (quantized 8-bit model variant or smaller decoder-only variant), and routing to a standby region.
- Fast failover path: health-check driven routing with automated routing changes within ~30-60s depending on connection state and cache warmup.
- Reserved capacity option: customers on Redwood Dedicated get pre-provisioned pools which remove cold-start variability and raise achievable SLA.
- Runbooks: automated escalation to SRE, immediate customer notification windows, and post-incident RCA templates.

Attachments included in this message (stubs):
- redwood-reliability-sla.pdf — draft SLA & SLO examples
- incident-summary-2025.csv — timeline and event tags (driver/regression, network, mitigation)

What we'll cover in the deep-dive
- Failover topology (region + model tier + caching), exact failover latencies we expect under different failure modes, and what Dedicated buys you vs hosted.
- Walk through runbook steps for the 2025 incidents and confirm telemetry you'll need for your RCA.

Thanks — I'll join the 6/10 slot if scheduled.

—Jonas
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
